snippet.title: Puerto Rico’s deadly drug addiction | Unreported World
snippet.description:
Unreported World is from Puerto Rico, a critical frontline in America’s war on drugs. Reporter Guillermo Galdos investigates how the island has become both a gateway for narcotics entering the United States and a victim of a devastating fentanyl epidemic.

As the U.S. pours billions into military operations across the Caribbean to seize the former President of Venezuela, and intercept drug shipments, federal agents on the island are stepping up raids against powerful gangs. Galdos joins the Drug Enforcement Administration and Police on high-risk operations in San Juan, where major arrests and drug seizures reveal the scale of the trade.

Efforts to stop trafficking are showing signs of deepening the crisis at home. On the streets, people are also battling addiction to fentanyl, a drug far more potent and dangerous than heroin. Outreach workers like Zuleika provide life-saving support to users. We meet young addicts like Eliot, trapped in cycles of dependency, and Tamara, who briefly seeks help but struggles to escape the grip of addiction.

While authorities focus on stopping supply, concerns mount that President Trump’s war on drugs in the Caribbean could be having unintended consequences.

Warning: This film shows strong images from the outset of the effects of serious drug abuse, which some viewers may find distressing.

snippet.description:

On the night of July 9, 1860, the schooner, Clotilda, disappears off of the coast of Alabama in Mobile Bay. Archaeologists attempt to learn if this wreck is the famed Clotilda, and the physical evidence it could provide on the dark history of the slave trade.

snippet.title: Danielle Deadwyler Traces the Power Behind Her Family Name | Finding Your Roots
snippet.description:
When I sat down with Danielle Deadwyler on Finding Your Roots, we followed her surname back nearly two centuries—to her third great-grandfather, Gaines Deadweiler, born in Georgia around 1840.

But what emerged was not simply a lineage—it was a choice. Danielle learned that her family name endured because her great-grandmother, Haddie, made the deliberate decision to pass on her own surname rather than adopt her husband’s. That act of self-definition, preserved across generations, remains embedded in Danielle’s identity today.

As Danielle reflected, names are more than inheritance—they are declarations. Like August Wilson typing his own name at the start of his artistic journey, Haddie’s decision reminds us that we each have the power to define how we move through the world.

snippet.title: New Discoveries Rewrite Maya History | Rise and Fall of the Maya MEGA Episode | National Geographic
snippet.description:
What actually happened to the ancient Maya? Mysteries unfold in this four episode Rise and Fall of the Maya Mega Episode compilation from National Geographic. Journey where the Maya lived in Mexico and Guatemala as archaeologists and historians uncover new evidence that rewrites what we know about this fascinating and mysterious ancient civilization. From the monumental discovery of a 3,000-year-old hidden megastructure to the puzzling, catastrophic collapse that forced millions to abandon their pyramid-filled cities, explore the origins of Maya power, secrets, and resilience in this documentary series. Featuring full episodes: 

Origins - 00:00 
What is Aguada Fénix? In June 2020, scientists discover Aguada Fénix, a monumental 3,000-year-old Maya structure. Uncover the hidden secrets of Aguada Fénix, the oldest monument built by the ancient Maya civilization, dating back to around 1000 BCE, that challenge everything we knew about the Maya's earliest days.

Civilization - 44:03 
New architectural and technological evidence unearthed in Mexico’s Yucatán Peninsula transforms long-held ideas about how the Maya civilization grew into a superpower.

Collapse - 01:28:06
Why did the ancient Maya civilization collapse? Many cities were abandoned due to a complex combination of severe droughts, overpopulation, deforestation, and warfare. The exact series of events that lead the ancient Maya to abandon their pyramid-filled cities has long puzzled archaeologists. Now, new investigations in Mexico and Guatemala are exposing surprising evidence about why these great monuments were deserted. 

Resilience - 02:12:09
Archaeologists unearth new clues about the resurgence of the ancient Maya civilization and the devastating events that would ultimately lead them to abandon their cities for good. Investigations also reveal evidence of extreme resilience in the face of catastrophe.

snippet.title: The Great Migration, Pogroms, and the Birth of the NAACP | Black and Jewish America | PBS
snippet.description:
Two historic migrations reshaped the relationship between Black and Jewish Americans in the early 20th century.

As millions of African Americans fled Jim Crow violence and economic hardship in the Great Migration, millions of Eastern European Jews escaped pogroms and persecution, sailing to the same northern cities. There, shared experiences of racial terror and exclusion began to foster new awareness and, in some cases, solidarity.

The 1908 Springfield, Illinois race riot—sparked by a false accusation and resulting in lynchings and widespread destruction—became a turning point. Journalists William English Walling and Anna Strunsky, deeply shaken by the violence, joined Black and white progressives in calling for a national organization to combat racial injustice. The result was the founding of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP), with significant Jewish participation in its early leadership and development.

All episodes of Black and Jewish America, hosted by Henry Louis Gates Jr., are streaming now on PBS and PBS.org.

localized.title: The Great Migration, Pogroms, and the Birth of the NAACP | Black and Jewish America | PBS
localized.description:
Two historic migrations reshaped the relationship between Black and Jewish Americans in the early 20th century.

As millions of African Americans fled Jim Crow violence and economic hardship in the Great Migration, millions of Eastern European Jews escaped pogroms and persecution, sailing to the same northern cities. There, shared experiences of racial terror and exclusion began to foster new awareness and, in some cases, solidarity.

The 1908 Springfield, Illinois race riot—sparked by a false accusation and resulting in lynchings and widespread destruction—became a turning point. Journalists William English Walling and Anna Strunsky, deeply shaken by the violence, joined Black and white progressives in calling for a national organization to combat racial injustice. The result was the founding of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP), with significant Jewish participation in its early leadership and development.

All episodes of Black and Jewish America, hosted by Henry Louis Gates Jr., are streaming now on PBS and PBS.org.

snippet.description:
Through new discoveries in science and archaeology, this episode explores the origins of the Vikings and how a great Viking dynasty changed history. It investigates who the Vikings were and why they left Scandinavia to plunder far-off lands. New scientific research suggests they were driven by an unstoppable force: climate change. In Norway, experts build replica Viking ships and explain the sailing technology that enabled long distance voyages. The Vikings continued raiding for decades. But eventually they began to establish more permanent settlements in Britain and Ireland, and in 2020 archaeologists discovered Dublin’s massive Viking harbour. A mighty king named Ivarr controlled this port, and he and his descendants built an empire in Britain and Ireland.

snippet.title: The Forgotten Massacre That Shocked the Allied Command | WW2 (No AI)
snippet.description:
What really happened at the Barn at La Plaine au Bois? Discover the harrowing true story of the Wormhoudt Massacre, where 80 British and French POWs were executed by the SS during the retreat to Dunkirk.

In May 1940, as the British Expeditionary Force (BEF) fought a desperate rearguard action to save the Allied army at Dunkirk, the soldiers of the 2nd Battalion, Royal Warwickshire Regiment, and the Cheshire Regiment stood their ground. After running out of ammunition, they surrendered—expecting the protection of the Geneva Convention. Instead, they were met by the Leibstandarte SS Adolf Hitler.

In this video, we investigate:

The Stand at Wormhoudt: How the 144th Infantry Brigade delayed the German advance for 48 vital hours

The Barn Atrocity: The brutal reality of the cowshed where grenades and machine guns were used against unarmed prisoners

The Survivors: The incredible escape of Bert Evans and the heroism of CSM Augustus Jennings.

snippet.title: Meet The Normans With Eleanor Janega: The Rise Of William The Conqueror
snippet.description:
They were the Northmen who changed history. Starting as heathen Viking warriors who plundered and settled in Northern France and forged the new Duchy of Normandy, becoming the most ferocious conquerors that medieval Europe had ever seen, and giving England its most famous date: 1066. In this two part series, Dr Eleanor Janega sets off across Normandy to discover who this band of rugged warriors, settlers and rulers were. In episode 2, Eleanor explores William’s precarious childhood and early military experience through the great castles and countryside of Normandy. By 1066, the Normans were hungry for more land and power, and William took advantage of tumultuous events across the channel to launch an invasion of England.

snippet.title: Kristin Chenoweth’s Unexpected ‘Wizard of Oz’ Family Connection | Finding Your Roots
snippet.description:
When I welcomed Kristin Chenoweth to Finding Your Roots, neither of us expected to uncover a theatrical twist worthy of Broadway itself.

In a small-town newspaper notice announcing a local production of The Wizard of Oz, we found the name of Kristin’s relative, Billy Eugene Ethridge, cast as none other than the Wizard. As Kristin quickly realized, this was more than coincidence. Growing up, Billy appeared in musical productions, sang in choirs, and immersed himself in performance—long before Kristin would take the stage herself.

Genealogy often reveals unexpected echoes across generations. Here, in black and white print, was a reminder that the love of music, theater, and performance can travel silently through a family tree, waiting for its next star to step into the spotlight.
